text:
incident-bot: HIGH severity paging — canary cluster 'canary-7828' showing sustained p95 token latency increase x3 after deploy v1.8.2 (rollout started 1769456500). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/inference/canary-latency
Alex (oncall): I'm on it. looking at metrics now.
Lee (SRE): I see increased kernel-fallback counts + eviction logs on nodes g4-05..g4-08. KPIs: p95 tokens up, throughput down.
Maya (runtime): Confirmed. Observed repeated kernel fallback to slow-path after commit that enabled "prefetch_v2" on the canary. Batching also collapsed — batch sizes went from ~12 to ~2.
Sam (releases): Rollout pushed at +10m, flag "prefetch_v2" enabled for canary only. No other changes. If kill switch exists we can flip.
Alex (oncall): Sam — can you flip the kill-flag and revert traffic to previous model variant? If not, I'll call rollback.
Sam (releases): Flipping feature flag now: `POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle?name=prefetch_v2&env=canary&value=off`
incident-bot: action logged — flag toggle requested by Sam at 1769456732.
Maya (runtime): After flip, I'm seeing immediate drop in kernel-fallbacks on pod canary-7828-3. Batch size slowly recovering.
Lee (SRE): Running `kubectl rollout restart deploy/canary-7828 -n canary` to ensure nodes pick new config.
Alex (oncall): Initiated rollback plan in case flip doesn't stabilize: 1) remove canary traffic 2) pin to previous model variant 3) open customer comms draft.
Jon (CS): Heads up — support queue showing ~3 customers reporting slow responses (tickets 4521, 4523). Not widespread but one enterprise customer hit 5xx. I'll prep comms if this persists >30m.
Rachel (PM): Which customers are affected? Any SLA breaches expected? Need ETA for recovery for outreach.
Maya (runtime): Affected requests correlated with long sequences >512 tokens and concurrent warm-up requests. Error rate increase ~0.6% peak. No known SLA breach yet but watch sensitive customers.
Lee (SRE): Metrics show steady improvement since flag flip. p95 dropping back toward baseline over last 3 mins. Continuing to monitor for KV cache warm-up.
Sam (releases): Confirmed flag toggle succeeded and no rollback needed at the moment. Leaving canary in reduced traffic mode for 20m for observation.
Alex (oncall): I'll keep the channel open. Sam, please keep the kill-switch handy and notify if anything spikes. Jon, keep CS looped with a short status update.
Jon (CS): Sent a brief to affected customers: "We observed increased latency in a canary rollout and have toggled the related optimization flag. We are monitoring — will update in 15 minutes."
incident-bot: NOTE: handoff scheduled at 1769457600 to APAC oncall. Add follow-up actions to postmortem checklist.
Rachel (PM): Please capture exact commit and flag change in the postmortem. We need a clear rollback criteria and a tighter canary ramp policy.
Alex (oncall): Summary: flag toggled off, restart performed, metrics improving, reducing canary traffic. Handoff planned. If we hit >1% error or p95 > baseline *1.8, we will rollback fully.
Maya (runtime): Adding diagnostic logs to the incident timeline:
```
[1769456660] kernel_fallback_count=124 node=g4-05 pod=canary-7828-3
[1769456700] batch_size=2 median
[1769456760] flag_prefetch_v2=OFF
```
Alex (oncall): Closing active mitigation loop. Leaving channel open for handoff and postmortem.
Sam (releases): Will create rollback revert PR and pause the rest of the rollout.
Lee (SRE): I'll collect kernel and eviction traces for the postmortem.
Jon (CS): Customers updated at 1769457000. No escalations so far.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — monitoring state. Tags: canary, feature-flag, kernel-fallback, paging, customer-impact.
